comments.body:
Debug-orchestrator session — checkpoint for compaction. Mandate: keep main green, investigate
CI/AWS errors, resolve orphan bugs, drive epic 6202 (disk) and the new telemetry epic. Orchestrator
role: board reads, decisions, ticket authoring, subagent briefs, submits, closes. All RCA/repair
delegated.

## PRODUCTION INCIDENT AND ITS ROOT CAUSE (proven)

Gerrit went fully offline 21:28-22:09 UTC 2026-09-04 (41 min). Recovered by an operator-authorised
stop/start. Root cause PROVEN experimentally via /rebar-debug, not inferred:

**H2 (sustainer):** `infra/scripts/observability.sh` performs **12 unbounded whole-journal scans per
run** (`:760, :788, :816, :976`, plus 8 unconditional `publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` calls at
`902,904,910,914,922,935,940,942` each scanning at `:883`). Its unit
(`install-observability.sh:20-27`) is `Type=oneshot` with **no `TimeoutStartSec`** — systemd reports
`TimeoutStartUSec=infinity` for such units — and `:31` sets `OnUnitActiveSec=5min`, computed from
the last COMPLETED activation. **A hung run does not delay the timer; it DELETES its next elapse**
(`NextElapseUSecMonotonic=infinity`, confirmed on real systemd 255). One overrun = permanent
silence, no self-recovery.

Measured (colima Ubuntu 24.04, cgroup v2 io.max throttled to gp3's 3,000 IOPS / 125 MB/s,
read_ahead_kb=16): a **1.86 GB** journal took **407.5 s = 136% of the 300 s period** at 2,985 IOPS /
48.2 MB/s. **Threshold: the period is exhausted at ~1.37 GB.** Control: same journal, unbounded
33,936 ms vs `-n 5000` 798 ms — **42.5x**; the field index does NOT reduce bytes read.

**INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION:** epic 6202 story S3, working a different ticket with no knowledge of
that threshold, measured the host's real journal at **1.7 GB** — above 1.37 GB, inside the confirmed
overrun band.

**H1 (trigger):** `container_memory_rss_bytes` (anon RSS; page cache cannot contaminate) shows mcp
swinging 0.52 -> 3.15 GB, at 3.02 GB at 14:25. Total anon ~4.16 GB of 8 GiB — NOT exhaustion. The
14:05-14:25 lull (8,333 reads/5min = ~28 IOPS) means the working set was cached; one allocation
evicted it, and every later scan went cold.

Explains all six constraints. The hardest — "publisher died BEFORE the storm" — dissolves: the
script publishes cheap metrics EARLY and does journal work LATE, so **the publisher ENTERED the
storm** and by the latch could never leave.

**Legitimacy: DEFECT against the script's OWN contract.** `:291-292` bounds its docker calls and
states the rule ("a wedged daemon under disk pressure must not hold the 5-minute timer open"),
restated `:545-551`. The 12 journal scans violate it; the unit violates it again by omitting
`TimeoutStartSec`.

Corrections to my own earlier claims, all recorded on ticket 1205: it is **12 scans not 11**;
"~3 concurrent readers" was over-read (Little's law: 2,585 IOPS x 1.035 ms = 2.68 — ONE sequential
scanner on a ~1 ms device); EBS degradation REFUTED; "climbing all afternoon" WRONG (reads fell to
8,333 then erupted); the journal was **already capped** at the 4 GiB default, so "unbounded journal"
was wrong — 12 unbounded SCANS of a correctly-capped journal is the fault, and no journald cap would
have prevented it.

## MERGED AND CLOSED THIS SESSION

Changes merged: 2622, 2623 (S2), 2630, 2631, 2632, 2642, 2643 (S3), 2644.
Tickets closed: 1ef8 (preexisting), 6f66 (obsolete — ACs provably unachievable), 87b8, 1738, 2862,
e956/S3. Epic 6202: S0, S1, S3, S6 closed; **S2 merged but NOT closed** (3 of 10 ACs describe
superseded mechanisms and need rewording first); S4, S5 open and unblocked.

## OPERATOR DECISIONS TAKEN

- 337e chromium -> **(b) loud intentional skip**. Dispatched.
- f850 Windows -> **(a) adopt as a support target**. Decomposition dispatched. `lock.py` FIRST
  (377/510 failures); the two-line fix is UNSAFE (makes `fcntl_held=True` a lie -> silent store
  corruption); do NOT flip the job to gating until the epic completes; ADR 0114 governs.
- Terraform apply AUTHORISED and DONE: 5 alarms added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed. Instance never
  cycled. `user_data` drift resolved by the recovery stop/start.
- Caps installed on the host: **journald cap IN FORCE**; **docker cap installed, NOT in force**
  (needs a scheduled `systemctl restart docker`).
- ae97 AC4 -> **the LaunchAgent SELF-REPORTS** (inverts the dependency; no rebar code knows
  LaunchAgents exist). Transport left to the implementer.
- b973 -> **reparented under janitor epic 78f2**; that session owns it (original scanner ticket
  aa9e-3d35-fd3e-41ee is still open). Any re-land follows **ADR 0114**: advisory first, one
  independent passing run on main, then promotion.
- bff5 AC3 -> closed as satisfied.
- Main checkout fast-forwarded 0fbbe517e360 -> e510c64dbcb6 (tree was clean).

## STILL FIRING / STILL NEEDED

`rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` — REAL: BuildKit cache 5,433,000,000 B vs its 5 GiB share =
101%. Already over the cap; the daemon's GC cannot reclaim until Docker restarts.
`rebar-docker-unaccounted-bytes` — real but inflated (see 81cc below).

**ONE ACTION CLOSES SEVERAL:** a scheduled `systemctl restart docker` puts the builder.gc cap in
force AND sweeps ~1.0 GB of orphaned overlay2 from the 09-02 outage. Cost: disrupts Gerrit, MCP,
review-bot.

The gate-scratch volume is attached but RAW. Mount deferred by operator decision until
`grapy-agronomic-sealion` (device-resolution guessing) is fixed — that fix is dispatched.

## TICKETS FILED THIS SESSION (all from executed evidence)

2a21 head_sha misleading | fd2b Drift fmt-before-plan | 9c64 CI parity gap | da05 main-health runs
mutually cancel | d614 resolve_ebs_device GUESSES on empty id (proven data destruction) | 9c93 no
`/var/gerrit` mount assertion | ad8d user_data hardening | a9d1 mirror alarm pages on healthy
operation | 9018 no off-box logs | ea66 three metrics dead 7+ days (alarms unfalsifiable;
`list-metrics` shows names, hiding it) | 1205 IOPS saturation | 16e1 nested-pytest evades the
uniqueness guard | 2862 hcl2 sibling | eebc stale-tree terraform "No changes" | ff4a attestation
persists an unverifiable signature | 81cc **docker_unaccounted_bytes unit-incommensurable — 56% of
the 2.5 GiB is xfs block overhead; will fire from rounding before the host hits its own budget; FIX
UNITS NOT THRESHOLD** | 5fb0 install-observability deploys only the probe, so cap scripts are
unreachable and `journal_cap_in_effect` publishes a FALSE 0 forever | 40e3 stash ban scoped to
ticket store only + `stash create` silently drops untracked files.

New epic: **80c4 pleasant-reliant-nandu** — "Observability that survives the host", children 9018
and ea66.

## THE RECURRING CLASS

Nearly every finding is **absence of execution reported as success**: a drift gate blinded by
whitespace before `plan` ran; a CI job voting green without executing; a test passing vacuously
because `tempfile.gettempdir()` memoised; a cap reporting "in effect" after a SIGHUP that does not
apply it; a probe silencing itself so absence read as health; `terraform plan` from a stale tree
saying "No changes"; a metric publishing a confident false 0. **The checks meant to catch problems
were themselves the problem.**

## IN FLIGHT AT CHECKPOINT

1205 attribution+repair | ff4a attestation /rebar-debug | d614 device-resolution fix | 337e chromium
| f850 Windows decomposition.

**BLOCKED, do not dispatch:** 81cc + ea66 + S4 + S5 (all need `observability.sh`, held by 1205);
9c93 + ad8d (need `user_data.sh`, held by d614); 16e1 (was waiting on the stash research — now
UNBLOCKED); 9c64 + eebc (conflict with 337e/da05 and fd2b).

**UNBLOCKED and ready:** 2a21, da05, fd2b, a1f1, 5246, 6a9d, 16e1.

**Concurrency discipline:** gate-running agents capped at ~4 (S6's admission cap); concurrent gate
+ full-suite load is the evidenced cause of tonight's outage and that fix has NOT landed. Agents are
briefed NOT to run `make verify` or a full `make test`.

## HOST FACTS WORTH KEEPING

`timeout` does not exist here (exit 127, silent no-op) — AGENTS.md now carries a `bound()` helper
(landed via 2630). `trap 'kill 0'` does not reap a wrapper. `pgrep -f` matches ITSELF. Four orphaned
processes reaped tonight, one at 61 CPU-minutes on a one-second sleep. Three stashes in the shared
stack hold another session's held-out TDD work — **never `git stash pop`/`drop` anywhere**.
